intent.raw_query: Swiss Alps ski holiday family, $7000, 7 days, February

experiences.name: Zermatt Ski Safari
experiences.description: Explore the world-renowned ski slopes of Zermatt with access to over 360km of pistes across Switzerland and Italy. Ski beneath the iconic Matterhorn with breathtaking panoramic views. Suitable for intermediate to advanced skiers with varied terrain including groomed runs and off-piste adventures.

experiences.name: Jungfrau Region Snowshoeing & Winter Hiking
experiences.description: Guided snowshoeing tour through the stunning Jungfrau region, trekking through pristine alpine landscapes, frozen lakes, and snow-covered forests. Visit the Aletsch Glacier viewpoint, the largest glacier in the Alps, and enjoy a traditional Swiss fondue lunch at a mountain hut along the trail.

experiences.name: St. Moritz Ice Skating & Bobsled Experience
experiences.description: Skate on the legendary frozen Lake St. Moritz and then experience the thrill of riding the historic Olympia Bob Run, one of the world's oldest natural ice bobsled tracks dating back to 1904. A unique adrenaline-pumping winter activity combining culture and sport in the glamorous St. Moritz setting.

experiences.name: Glacier 3000 Suspension Bridge & Peak Walk
experiences.description: Take the cable car up to Glacier 3000 and walk across the Peak Walk by Tissot, the world's first suspension bridge connecting two mountain peaks at 3,000 meters altitude. Enjoy 360-degree views of 24 Alpine peaks including Mont Blanc and the Matterhorn, and optionally try the glacier ski area or snow bus ride.

experiences.name: Traditional Swiss Alpine Cuisine & Cheese Cellar Tour
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in authentic Swiss mountain culture with a guided visit to a traditional alpine cheese cellar in the Appenzell region, learning how Gruyère and Raclette are crafted. Follow with a hands-on fondue and raclette cooking class paired with local Swiss wines and schnapps in a cozy chalet setting.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Swiss Alps, Switzerland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Zurich or Milan Malpensa airport at 22:30. Take a regional train or bus toward Poschiavo. Check in to B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama upon late arrival. Settle in, unpack, and rest for the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In transit
meals.lunch: N/A - In transit
meals.dinner: Grab a quick sandwich or snack at the airport arrivals hall or a vending machine (~CHF 8-12). Most restaurants will be closed upon late arrival in Poschiavo.

day_by_day.notes: Poschiavo is best reached via the Bernina Express rail line from St. Moritz or by bus from Tirano (Italy). Pre-book your train ticket in advance on SBB.ch for best budget fares. The journey from Zurich takes approximately 3.5-4 hours. Confirm check-in arrangements with the B&B for late arrival. Keep CHF cash on hand as rural areas may have limited card acceptance.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a hearty B&B breakfast included with your stay. Afterward, take a leisurely walk through the charming historic village of Poschiavo — explore the Piazza Comunale, the Spanish Quarter (Quartiere Spagnolo), and the Collegiate Church of San Vittore. This orientation walk is completely free and gives you a feel for the local Romansh-Italian culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearby Lago di Poschiavo (Lake Poschiavo), a scenic frozen or semi-frozen alpine lake in winter. Walk along the lakeside path (~3 km loop, free). If conditions allow, enjoy the stunning mountain reflections and snow-covered surroundings. Visit the local Coop supermarket in Poschiavo to stock up on budget groceries, snacks, and water for the week.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the B&B and relax. Explore the village in the early evening — the illuminated historic buildings are beautiful in winter. Plan your ski days for the rest of the week by researching Diavolezza and Corvatsch ski areas accessible via the Bernina Express.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B Berninahaus Panorama — enjoy local bread, cheese, cold cuts, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Self-catered picnic with groceries from Coop Poschiavo — bread, local cheese, salami, and fruit (~CHF 8-10).
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using B&B kitchen facilities if available, or try Ristorante Croce Federale in Poschiavo for a budget pasta or risotto dish (~CHF 18-22). Ask for the daily special (piatto del giorno) for best value.

day_by_day.notes: Poschiavo sits at 1,014m elevation. Dress in warm layers even in the village. The Bernina Express scenic railway passes through Poschiavo — a free visual treat from the platform. Exchange currency or use ATMs in the village center. Budget tip: buy a 7-day Swiss Half Fare Card or regional Engadin pass for discounted train travel.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Bernina Express train from Poschiavo toward Pontresina/St. Moritz (approx. 45-60 min, ~CHF 15-20 one way with Half Fare Card). Head to Diavolezza ski area — one of the most spectacular and budget-accessible ski resorts in the Engadin valley. Purchase a day ski pass (~CHF 55-65 with discounts). Ski the wide open glacier runs on Diavolezza with breathtaking views of Piz Palü and Morteratsch Glacier.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing at Diavolezza. Try the famous Diavolezza-Lagalb traverse run if conditions permit — a classic 10km off-piste route (guide recommended). Alternatively, stick to groomed blue and red pistes for intermediate skiers. Take a break at the mid-mountain restaurant terrace with packed lunch to save money.
day_by_day.evening: Return by train to Poschiavo. Warm up with a hot drink at the B&B. Rest tired muscles and prepare gear for the next ski day.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B — fuel up well before a full ski day.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from B&B or Coop — sandwiches, energy bars, thermos of hot tea (~CHF 5-8). Mountain restaurant prices are very high (CHF 20-35 per meal), so packing lunch saves significantly.
meals.dinner: Trattoria da Reto or a local pizzeria in Poschiavo — pizza or pasta (~CHF 16-20). Alternatively, self-cater with pasta and local sauce from Coop (~CHF 5-7).

day_by_day.notes: Diavolezza ski pass: check for online early-booking discounts at diavolezza.ch. Ski rental in Poschiavo or Pontresina is cheaper than at the resort base — budget ~CHF 30-40/day for skis, boots, and poles. Bring your own helmet if possible. The Bernina Express train schedule is limited — check SBB.ch for exact times and book ahead. Dress in full waterproof ski gear; temperatures at 3,000m can drop to -15°C or below.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning — allow muscles to recover. After B&B breakfast, take a snowshoe hike from Poschiavo toward the Alp Grüm area. The trail from Poschiavo station up toward Alp Grüm (accessible also by Bernina Express) offers stunning winter panoramas over the Valposchiavo valley. Snowshoe rental available locally (~CHF 15-20/day).
day_by_day.afternoon: Board the Bernina Express to Alp Grüm station (one of the most scenic stops in Europe, ~CHF 10-15 with Half Fare Card). Walk the short snowshoe loop around Alp Grüm with views of Palü Glacier. Visit the historic Ristorante Alp Grüm for a warm drink (hot chocolate ~CHF 5). Return to Poschiavo by train in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Poschiavo's evening atmosphere. Visit the local Enoteca or wine bar for a glass of Valtellina red wine — the valley's famous Nebbiolo-based wine produced just across the Italian border (~CHF 5-8/glass). Early night to prepare for another ski day.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the snowshoe trail — thermos soup, sandwiches, chocolate (~CHF 5-8).
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at B&B — buy local Pizzoccheri pasta (a Valtellina buckwheat specialty) from Coop and cook it yourself (~CHF 6-8 for ingredients). This is an authentic regional dish and very budget-friendly.

day_by_day.notes: Alp Grüm sits at 2,091m and offers one of the most dramatic viewpoints on the Bernina line. The snowshoe trails are generally well-marked but check local conditions at the Poschiavo tourist office (free maps available). This is a great low-cost active day that showcases the alpine scenery without ski pass expenses. Bring trekking poles for stability on icy paths.

day_by_day.morning: Second ski day — take the Bernina Express to Pontresina and connect to Corvatsch or Corviglia ski areas above St. Moritz. Corviglia is more budget-friendly and beginner-to-intermediate friendly. Day pass ~CHF 60-70 (check for online discounts). Enjoy wide groomed pistes with views over the Engadin lakes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing at Corviglia. Try the long Marguns run back to Celerina for a scenic descent. If budget allows, take the cable car up to Piz Nair (3,057m) for panoramic views of the entire Upper Engadin valley — even non-skiers can appreciate this viewpoint.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by Bernina Express. Treat yourself to a sit-down dinner to celebrate the halfway point of your trip. Try the local Grotto-style restaurant in Poschiavo for authentic Graubünden cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B — eat extra to fuel the ski day.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch again to save on mountain restaurant costs (~CHF 5-8). Find a sunny terrace spot on the mountain to enjoy your meal with a view.
meals.dinner: Grotto-style dinner at a local Poschiavo restaurant — try Capuns (Swiss chard rolls with spätzle) or Maluns (potato dish) for authentic Graubünden flavors (~CHF 20-25 including a local beer or wine).

day_by_day.notes: St. Moritz is one of the world's most famous ski resorts but can be visited on a budget by focusing on skiing and avoiding the luxury shops and restaurants. The ski areas are world-class regardless of budget. Consider a 2-day ski pass if planning to ski both Day 3 and Day 5 — multi-day passes offer better value (~CHF 100-115 for 2 days vs CHF 55-65 x2). Keep receipts for any VAT refund eligibility.

day_by_day.morning: Active rest day with a winter hike. From Poschiavo, take the local PostBus toward Le Prese (a small spa village on Lake Poschiavo, ~10 min, ~CHF 3-4). Walk the flat lakeside path from Le Prese back to Poschiavo (~5 km, 1.5 hours) — a beautiful and easy winter walk along the frozen lake shore with views of the surrounding peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Poschiavo Museum (Museo di Poschiavo) to learn about the valley's unique history, the Spanish Quarter heritage, and local Romansh-Italian culture (~CHF 5 entry). Afterward, browse the local artisan shops for budget souvenirs — local honey, Bündner Nusstorte (nut tart), and dried meats make excellent affordable gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk up to the viewpoint above Poschiavo village for panoramic views of the valley and surrounding 3,000m peaks glowing in alpenglow. Return for a final relaxed evening at the B&B — pack bags and prepare for departure day.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B.
meals.lunch: Bakery lunch in Poschiavo — fresh bread, local cheese, and a pastry from the village bakery (~CHF 8-10).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner — splurge slightly at a local restaurant for a full Graubünden menu: Bündnerfleisch (air-dried beef) starter, Maluns or Capuns main, and Bündner Nusstorte dessert (~CHF 28-35). This is your last full evening — worth the treat!

day_by_day.notes: Saturday markets may be available in Poschiavo — check locally for fresh produce and artisan stalls. The lakeside walk is flat and suitable for all fitness levels. Le Prese also has a small thermal spa (Terme di Poschiavo) if you want to soothe ski-tired muscles (~CHF 20-25 for 2 hours) — a worthwhile splurge on a rest day. Buy any last souvenirs today as Sunday shops may be closed.

day_by_day.morning: Final B&B breakfast — enjoy it leisurely. Take one last walk through Poschiavo's historic center to say goodbye to this hidden gem of the Swiss Alps. Visit the Sunday morning church service at the Collegiate Church of San Vittore if interested — a beautiful baroque interior and a unique cultural experience (free).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of B&B and begin journey home. Take the Bernina Express northbound toward St. Moritz and Chur, or southbound toward Tirano (Italy) depending on your departure airport. The Bernina Express itself is a UNESCO World Heritage railway — enjoy the spectacular scenery of the Bernina Pass (2,253m), the Brusio spiral viaduct, and the glacial landscapes as a final alpine farewell.
day_by_day.evening: Continue travel to departure airport (Zurich ~4 hours, Milan Malpensa ~2.5 hours via Tirano). Allow ample time for check-in and security. Reflect on an incredible budget week in the Swiss Alps!

meals.breakfast: Final included B&B breakfast — eat well for the travel day.
meals.lunch: Pack remaining groceries from Coop for a train picnic — the Bernina Express journey is so scenic you won't want to leave your seat anyway (~CHF 5-8).
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal. If departing from Milan Malpensa, grab a budget Italian meal in Tirano before boarding (~€10-12 for pasta and a drink — much cheaper than Swiss prices).

day_by_day.notes: The Bernina Express is one of the world's great train journeys — even on a regular regional ticket (not the panoramic tourist version) the views are extraordinary. Sit on the right side heading north for the best glacier views. Confirm your return train booking on SBB.ch well in advance, especially on Sundays when services may be reduced. Luggage storage is available at major stations if needed. Total estimated budget for 7 days (excluding flights): CHF 600-750 per person, including accommodation, ski passes (2 days), food, and transport.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival. Flight UA lands at 22:30. Transfer from airport to B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama. Check in, settle into your room, and get a good night's rest.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — travel day.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama around 23:30–00:00 depending on transfer. Grab a light snack if available at the B&B or from any provisions you carry. Rest and prepare for the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit or airport dining
meals.dinner: Light snack at the B&B upon arrival or airport meal before departure. Keep it simple — a sandwich or soup from the airport.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange your transfer from the airport to Poschiavo in advance as it is a remote alpine village. The drive from Zurich or Milan Malpensa (closest major airports) to Poschiavo takes approximately 2.5–3 hours. Confirm B&B late check-in arrangements ahead of time. Pack light layers for the cold alpine night.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely start after your late arrival. After breakfast at the B&B, take a gentle orientation walk through the charming historic village of Poschiavo. Explore the Piazza Comunale, the Spanish Quarter (Quartiere Spagnolo), and the Church of San Vittore. Get acquainted with the local alpine atmosphere and pick up any winter gear or supplies you may need from local shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearby Lago di Poschiavo (Lake Poschiavo), a stunning frozen or partially frozen alpine lake in winter. Take a scenic walk along the lakeside trail, enjoying panoramic views of the surrounding snow-capped peaks. If conditions allow, try ice skating on the lake or simply soak in the serene winter landscape. This is a perfect low-key afternoon to recover from jet lag while immersing yourself in the Swiss Alps environment.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo village for a relaxed evening. Stroll through the illuminated old town and enjoy the quiet alpine charm. Visit a local café for a warm Glühwein (mulled wine) or hot chocolate before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama — enjoy local bread, cheese, cold cuts, and coffee included with your stay.
meals.lunch: Ristorante Suisse in Poschiavo — a mid-range local restaurant offering traditional Graubünden cuisine. Try the Pizzoccheri (buckwheat pasta with cheese and vegetables) or a hearty alpine soup. Budget: CHF 20–35.
meals.dinner: Ristorante Croce Federale in Poschiavo — cozy local trattoria with Romansh and Italian-Swiss dishes. Try the Capretto (roasted kid goat) or polenta with local cheese. Budget: CHF 35–55 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Poschiavo sits in the Valposchiavo valley at about 1,014m elevation. Dress warmly in layers. February temperatures can range from -5°C to +5°C. This is a recovery and orientation day — keep it relaxed. The village has a unique Italian-Swiss cultural blend due to its proximity to the Italian border, making it a charming and distinctive base.

day_by_day.morning: Embark on the Traditional Swiss Alpine Cuisine & Cheese Cellar Tour. Travel to a nearby alpine cheese producer in the Graubünden region (approximately 30–60 minutes from Poschiavo). Enjoy a guided tour of a traditional alpine cheese cellar, learning about centuries-old cheese-making techniques, the role of alpine pastures, and the art of aging Swiss mountain cheeses like Graubünden Bergkäse. Taste a variety of local cheeses paired with regional breads and cured meats.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the cheese tour, drive the scenic Bernina Pass road (if open and accessible) or take the famous Bernina Express train for a short segment to enjoy the dramatic winter alpine scenery. The Bernina Pass at 2,328m offers breathtaking views of glaciers, frozen lakes, and snow-covered peaks. Stop at Ospizio Bernina for photos and a short walk around the iconic Lago Bianco (White Lake), which is frozen solid in February.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo for the evening. Visit a local wine bar or enoteca to sample Valposchiavo wines — the region produces surprisingly good reds including Merlot and Pinot Noir. Enjoy a quiet dinner back in the village.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama.
meals.lunch: Included as part of the Swiss Alpine Cuisine & Cheese Cellar Tour — a traditional alpine spread of cheeses, charcuterie, bread, and local accompaniments.
meals.dinner: Osteria Salis in Poschiavo — intimate local osteria with excellent regional wines and seasonal alpine dishes. Try the venison ragù or risotto with local mushrooms. Budget: CHF 40–60 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Traditional Swiss Alpine Cuisine & Cheese Cellar Tour in advance. The Bernina Pass road (Route 29) may be closed in winter — check conditions before driving. The Bernina Express train is a reliable and scenic alternative and runs year-round. Dress in very warm layers for the Bernina Pass stop as temperatures at altitude can be significantly colder.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to St. Moritz for the St. Moritz Ice Skating & Bobsled Experience. Depart early from Poschiavo — St. Moritz is approximately 45–60 minutes away via the Bernina Pass or through the Engadin valley. Arrive at the legendary frozen Lake St. Moritz and lace up your skates for an unforgettable ice skating session on one of the world's most famous natural ice rinks. The lake backdrop with the Engadin mountains is absolutely spectacular in February.
day_by_day.afternoon: After skating, head to the historic Olympia Bob Run St. Moritz–Celerina — the world's oldest natural ice bobsled track, built in 1904. Experience the thrill of riding the bobsled as a passenger with a professional pilot, reaching speeds of up to 130 km/h on the natural ice track. This is a once-in-a-lifetime winter sports experience. Book your bobsled slot in advance as spots fill up quickly. Afterward, explore the glamorous St. Moritz village, window-shop on the Via Serlas, and enjoy the upscale alpine atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in St. Moritz before returning to Poschiavo. St. Moritz offers excellent mid-range dining options alongside its famous luxury establishments.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at B&B before departure.
meals.lunch: Restaurant Engiadina in St. Moritz — a beloved local institution serving traditional Engadin cuisine at reasonable prices. Try the Maluns (potato dish) or Bündner Gerstensuppe (barley soup). Budget: CHF 25–40.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Hauser in St. Moritz — a classic mid-range option with a warm atmosphere, serving Swiss and international dishes. Known for their excellent pastries and hearty mains. Budget: CHF 40–65 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Olympia Bob Run experience costs approximately CHF 150–250 per person — book well in advance at bobrun.ch. Ice skating on Lake St. Moritz is weather-dependent; skate rentals are available on-site. St. Moritz is a luxury resort town — budget accordingly for any additional shopping or activities. Return drive to Poschiavo takes about 45–60 minutes; plan to leave St. Moritz by 19:00–20:00.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to Zermatt for the Zermatt Ski Safari. Depart early from Poschiavo — Zermatt is approximately 2.5–3 hours away by car and train (drive to Visp or Täsch, then take the train to car-free Zermatt). Arrive and join the guided Zermatt Ski Safari, exploring the world-renowned ski slopes with access to over 360km of pistes. Ski under the iconic shadow of the Matterhorn on perfectly groomed runs. The safari guide will take you through the best runs suited to your skill level, from the gentle Sunnegga slopes to the more challenging Klein Matterhorn descents.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Zermatt Ski Safari through the afternoon, exploring different sectors of the vast ski area. Take the Glacier Express cable car up to Klein Matterhorn (3,883m) — the highest cable car station in the Alps — for extraordinary views and high-altitude skiing on the glacier. Enjoy a mid-afternoon break at one of the iconic mountain restaurants on the slopes.
day_by_day.evening: Après-ski in Zermatt village before beginning the return journey to Poschiavo. Zermatt's car-free village is magical in the evening with its twinkling lights and cozy atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at B&B before departure.
meals.lunch: Chez Vrony on the Findeln slope — one of Zermatt's most beloved mountain restaurants with stunning Matterhorn views. Try the rösti or the daily alpine special. Budget: CHF 35–55.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Whymper-Stube in Zermatt — a cozy, mid-range fondue and raclette restaurant named after the first Matterhorn climber. Perfect après-ski dining. Budget: CHF 40–60 per person. (Eat before the return journey or grab a train snack.)

day_by_day.notes: This is a long travel day — depart Poschiavo by 06:30–07:00 to maximize ski time. Ski rental equipment is available in Zermatt if you don't have your own. A day ski pass for Zermatt costs approximately CHF 85–100. The Zermatt Ski Safari experience should be booked in advance. Zermatt is car-free — park at Täsch (CHF 15/day) and take the shuttle train (10 minutes). Return to Poschiavo by 22:00–23:00.

day_by_day.morning: After the big Zermatt day, enjoy a slightly later start. Head to the Glacier 3000 Suspension Bridge & Peak Walk experience near Les Diablerets (approximately 2.5 hours from Poschiavo via Sion). Take the cable car up to Glacier 3000 at 3,000m elevation and walk across the iconic Peak Walk by Tissot — the world's first suspension bridge connecting two mountain peaks. The views of the Alps, including Mont Blanc, the Matterhorn, and the Eiger, are absolutely breathtaking on a clear day.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Peak Walk, enjoy the other activities at Glacier 3000: try the Snow Bus (a thrilling ride across the glacier), the Alpine Coaster (a toboggan run), or simply ski/snowboard on the glacier slopes. The glacier offers excellent snow conditions in February. Spend 2–3 hours exploring the glacier plateau before taking the cable car back down.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the return journey to Poschiavo. Stop in a village along the route (such as Sion or Brig) for dinner before the final drive back to your B&B.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama.
meals.lunch: Restaurant at Glacier 3000 summit — the Botta 3000 restaurant designed by architect Mario Botta offers stunning panoramic views. Try the alpine soup or mountain platter. Budget: CHF 30–50.
meals.dinner: Restaurant du Soleil in Sion (en route back) — a welcoming mid-range restaurant serving Valais specialties including raclette, fondue, and local Valais wines. Budget: CHF 35–55 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Glacier 3000 cable car tickets cost approximately CHF 45–65 per person return. The Peak Walk is included in the cable car ticket. Check weather forecasts carefully — visibility is crucial for the Peak Walk experience. The Snow Bus and Alpine Coaster have additional costs (CHF 10–20 each). This is another long travel day — consider whether to split the Glacier 3000 visit with a shorter Zermatt day or adjust based on energy levels.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Swiss Alps. Enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at the B&B, savoring the mountain views from Poschiavo Panorama. Pack your bags and take a final walk through Poschiavo village. Visit the local market if it's running on Sunday, pick up some Swiss souvenirs — local cheeses, Bündner Fleisch (air-dried beef), chocolate, and regional wines to take home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy the Jungfrau Region Snowshoeing & Winter Hiking experience as a final alpine adventure (note: this requires travel to the Jungfrau region, approximately 2.5–3 hours from Poschiavo — adjust timing based on your departure flight). Alternatively, if time is limited, enjoy a final snowshoe walk closer to Poschiavo in the local Valposchiavo valley trails. Rent snowshoes from a local sports shop and explore the pristine winter landscape around the village and lake on your own.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Poschiavo to celebrate a wonderful week in the Swiss Alps. Reflect on the incredible experiences — from Zermatt's slopes to Glacier 3000's peaks. Begin departure preparations if flying out the next day.

meals.breakfast: Final full breakfast at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama — enjoy every last bite of the Swiss alpine spread.
meals.lunch: Café del Dazio in Poschiavo — a charming local café with homemade pastries, sandwiches, and light alpine fare. Perfect for a relaxed final lunch. Budget: CHF 15–25.
meals.dinner: Ristorante Suisse in Poschiavo — return to this local favorite for a proper farewell dinner. Order the full Graubünden tasting menu if available, with local wine pairings. Budget: CHF 45–65 per person.

day_by_day.notes: If your return flight departs the next day, use this evening to fully pack and organize. If the Jungfrau Snowshoeing tour is a priority, consider doing it on Day 6 instead of Glacier 3000, or rearrange the itinerary accordingly. Tip: Purchase a Swiss Travel Pass for the week to save on train and cable car costs — it can reduce transportation expenses by 30–50%. Total estimated mid-range budget for the week (excluding flights and accommodation): CHF 1,200–1,800 per person.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

Visit the Aletsch Glacier viewpoint, the largest glacier in the Alps, and enjoy a traditional Swiss fondue lunch at a mountain hut along the trail.

experiences.name: St. Moritz Ice Skating & Bobsled Experience
experiences.description: Skate on the legendary frozen Lake St. Moritz and then experience the thrill of riding the historic Olympia Bob Run, one of the world's oldest natural ice bobsled tracks dating back to 1904. A unique adrenaline-pumping winter activity combining culture and sport in the glamorous St. Moritz setting.

experiences.name: Glacier 3000 Suspension Bridge & Peak Walk
experiences.description: Take the cable car up to Glacier 3000 and walk across the Peak Walk by Tissot, the world's first suspension bridge connecting two mountain peaks at 3,000 meters altitude. Enjoy 360-degree views of 24 Alpine peaks including Mont Blanc and the Matterhorn, and optionally try the glacier ski area or snow bus ride.

experiences.name: Traditional Swiss Alpine Cuisine & Cheese Cellar Tour
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in authentic Swiss mountain culture with a guided visit to a traditional alpine cheese cellar in the Appenzell region, learning how Gruyère and Raclette are crafted. Follow with a hands-on fondue and raclette cooking class paired with local Swiss wines and schnapps in a cozy chalet setting.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival. Flight UA lands at 22:30. Transfer from airport to B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama via private luxury transfer service. Check-in, unwind, and enjoy a welcome amenity prepared by the property.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — travel day.
day_by_day.evening: Late-night arrival at 22:30. Light in-room dining or a warm nightcap at the B&B. Settle in and rest to prepare for the week ahead in the Swiss Alps.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (travel day)
meals.lunch: Not applicable (travel day)
meals.dinner: In-room late-night snack platter arranged by the B&B — local cheeses, charcuterie, fresh bread, and herbal tea or a glass of Graubünden Pinot Noir

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private luxury transfer (Mercedes V-Class or similar) from the airport to Poschiavo. The drive from Zurich or Milan Malpensa to Poschiavo is approximately 2.5–3 hours. Confirm transfer timing with your concierge in advance. Pack light layers for the cold alpine arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the B&B with panoramic alpine views over the Bernina Pass. After breakfast, take a scenic private drive or the historic Bernina Express train toward St. Moritz (approximately 45 minutes from Poschiavo). Begin the St. Moritz Ice Skating & Bobsled Experience — skate on the legendary frozen Lake St. Moritz under crisp alpine skies, followed by an exhilarating ride on the historic Cresta Run or Olympic Bobsled track.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the glamorous village of St. Moritz at leisure. Browse luxury boutiques along Via Serlas, or visit the Segantini Museum for stunning alpine art. Enjoy a private guided snowshoe walk around the frozen lake perimeter with a local mountain guide for a more intimate alpine experience.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a top St. Moritz restaurant before returning to Poschiavo by private transfer. St. Moritz offers some of Switzerland's finest dining options for a memorable first full evening.

meals.breakfast: Full alpine breakfast at B&B Berninahaus — fresh pastries, local honey, Engadine nut tart, cold cuts, regional cheeses, and freshly brewed coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Mathis Food Affairs (St. Moritz) — a beloved alpine restaurant with panoramic terrace views and refined Swiss-Italian cuisine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurant Acla da Fans or La Marmite (St. Moritz) — indulge in Engadine specialties such as Bündner Gerstensuppe (barley soup), venison, and house-made pasta paired with local Graubünden wines

day_by_day.notes: The Bernina Express from Poschiavo to St. Moritz is a UNESCO World Heritage railway journey — a spectacular experience in itself. Book first-class panoramic seats in advance. Alternatively, arrange a private chauffeured vehicle for maximum flexibility. Bobsled experience must be pre-booked; check availability for the Cresta Run (members/guests only) or the public Olympic Bob Run.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure by private luxury transfer to Zermatt (approximately 3–3.5 hours from Poschiavo via Chur or the scenic Glacier Express route). Arrive in Zermatt — a car-free alpine paradise beneath the iconic Matterhorn. Begin the Zermatt Ski Safari with a certified private ski guide. Access over 360km of world-class pistes across Switzerland and Italy, starting with the legendary Klein Matterhorn runs at 3,883m — the highest ski area in the Alps.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Zermatt Ski Safari through the Rothorn and Sunnegga Paradise sectors. Enjoy off-piste powder runs with your guide if conditions allow. Take a scenic gondola to the Matterhorn Glacier Paradise for breathtaking 360-degree views of 38 Alpine peaks.
day_by_day.evening: Après-ski at the iconic Vernissage Bar or Papperla Pub in Zermatt village. Enjoy a fondue or raclette dinner in a cozy mountain chalet restaurant before the private transfer back to Poschiavo.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the B&B before early departure — grab-and-go option with pastries, fruit, and thermos coffee arranged by the property
meals.lunch: On-mountain lunch at Chez Vrony (Findeln, Zermatt) — one of the most celebrated mountain restaurants in the Alps, with stunning Matterhorn views and refined Swiss cuisine including rösti, truffle dishes, and local wines
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurant Zum See (Zermatt) — a legendary alpine hut restaurant accessible by ski or snowcat, serving exquisite seasonal menus with game, truffles, and fine Swiss wines in a candlelit rustic setting

day_by_day.notes: Zermatt is car-free — arrange an electric taxi from Täsch (the last car-accessible village) into Zermatt. Ski equipment rental at the highest level (Stöckli, Völkl, or custom-fit) is available through premium rental shops in Zermatt. Book Chez Vrony and Zum See well in advance as they are extremely popular. Consider an overnight stay in Zermatt to avoid the long return transfer — luxury options include The Omnia or Mont Cervin Palace.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at the B&B with a slow, indulgent breakfast. Take a gentle morning walk through the charming village of Poschiavo — a beautifully preserved Romansh-Italian border town with baroque architecture, the historic Piazza Comunale, and the Spanish Quarter. Visit the local market if available for artisan products.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart for the Glacier 3000 Suspension Bridge & Peak Walk experience (approximately 2.5 hours from Poschiavo via Aigle or Gstaad direction). Take the cable car up to Glacier 3000 (3,000m altitude) and walk across the Peak Walk by Tissot — the world's first suspension bridge connecting two mountain peaks. Enjoy panoramic views of Mont Blanc, the Matterhorn, and the Eiger. Optional: try the Alpine Coaster or snow bus on the glacier.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward Poschiavo or stop for dinner in the Gstaad or Château-d'Oex area — one of Switzerland's most exclusive alpine resort towns — before the scenic drive back.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely full breakfast at the B&B — Engadine specialties, bircher muesli, local jams, smoked salmon, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Peak Restaurant on Glacier 3000 — panoramic glass-enclosed dining with sweeping glacier views; enjoy Swiss classics like cheese soup, mountain charcuterie boards, and warm apple strudel
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurant Chesery (Gstaad) — a Michelin-starred institution offering refined French-Swiss cuisine in an elegant chalet setting, with an exceptional wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Glacier 3000 is located above Les Diablerets in the Vaud Alps — plan for a full-day excursion. The Peak Walk is weather-dependent; check conditions in advance. Dress in full thermal layers as temperatures at 3,000m can be extreme. The drive back to Poschiavo in the evening is scenic but long — consider hiring a private driver for the day for comfort and safety on mountain roads.

day_by_day.morning: Depart for the Jungfrau Region (approximately 2.5–3 hours from Poschiavo). Begin the Jungfrau Region Snowshoeing & Winter Hiking experience with a certified alpine guide. Trek through pristine snow-covered landscapes around Grindelwald or Mürren, with dramatic views of the Eiger North Face, Mönch, and Jungfrau. The guided tour takes you through untouched alpine terrain, frozen waterfalls, and silent winter forests.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the Jungfraujoch cogwheel train — the 'Top of Europe' at 3,454m — for a once-in-a-lifetime alpine experience. Visit the Ice Palace carved inside the Aletsch Glacier, the Sphinx Observatory, and enjoy panoramic views across the longest glacier in the Alps. Optional: try the Snowpark or zip line at Jungfraujoch.
day_by_day.evening: Descend to Grindelwald or Interlaken for a celebratory dinner at one of the region's finest restaurants before the return transfer to Poschiavo.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the B&B before departure — hearty alpine spread with eggs, local meats, cheeses, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Crystal Restaurant at Jungfraujoch (Top of Europe) — a unique dining experience at 3,454m with panoramic glacier views and a curated Swiss menu
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurant Schmitte (Grindelwald) or Taverne (Interlaken) — elegant Swiss-Alpine cuisine featuring Bernese specialties such as Berner Platte, lake fish, and seasonal game, paired with Bernese wines

day_by_day.notes: Book Jungfraujoch tickets well in advance — this is one of Switzerland's most popular attractions and sells out quickly, especially in peak winter season. The snowshoeing tour should be arranged through a certified Jungfrau Region guide service. Altitude sickness can affect some visitors at Jungfraujoch — take time to acclimatize and stay hydrated. The return drive to Poschiavo is approximately 3 hours; a private driver is strongly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Immerse yourself in authentic Swiss mountain culture with the Traditional Swiss Alpine Cuisine & Cheese Cellar Tour. Visit a traditional alpine cheese dairy (Käserei) in the Graubünden region near Poschiavo or the Engadine Valley. Watch master cheesemakers craft Graubünden mountain cheese, taste aged varieties, and learn about centuries-old alpine dairy traditions. Follow with a guided visit to a local wine cellar featuring Graubünden Pinot Noir — one of Switzerland's finest wine regions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Poschiavo area for a relaxed afternoon. Explore the Val Poschiavo valley on a private guided snowshoe walk or a scenic horse-drawn sleigh ride through the snow-covered valley floor — a quintessentially Swiss alpine experience. Alternatively, enjoy a private spa session if available at the B&B or a nearby wellness facility.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Poschiavo or the nearby Engadine Valley — celebrate the penultimate evening of the trip with a special multi-course dinner featuring the finest local ingredients discovered throughout the week.

meals.breakfast: Relaxed breakfast at the B&B — enjoy the full spread one more time with local specialties and panoramic Bernina Pass views
meals.lunch: Lunch included as part of the Cheese Cellar Tour — a traditional alpine spread of freshly made cheese fondue, raclette, cured meats, pickles, and dark rye bread paired with local wines
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ristorante Suisse (Poschiavo) or a private chef dinner arranged at the B&B — a curated 5-course tasting menu featuring Graubünden specialties: Bündner Nusstorte, venison ragù, truffle polenta, and a selection of regional wines and digestifs

day_by_day.notes: The cheese cellar tour should be pre-arranged with a local agritourism operator in the Graubünden region. Horse-drawn sleigh rides in Val Poschiavo can be booked through local operators — a magical experience at dusk with the Bernina peaks glowing in alpenglow. Consider purchasing artisan cheese, local wines, and Bündner Nusstorte as premium gifts to take home.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Swiss Alps. Enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at the B&B with sweeping views of the Bernina Pass. Take a short, peaceful morning walk through Poschiavo village to soak in the last moments of alpine tranquility. Visit the historic Reformed Church of San Vittore or simply sit in the Piazza Comunale with a final espresso.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the B&B and depart by private luxury transfer to the airport (Zurich approximately 3 hours, Milan Malpensa approximately 2.5 hours). If time permits before departure, stop at a premium Swiss chocolate shop or delicatessen in Chur or along the route for last-minute luxury souvenirs — Läderach or Sprüngli chocolates, aged Graubünden cheese, and local Pinot Noir.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Switzerland. Reflect on an extraordinary week of world-class skiing, breathtaking alpine landscapes, gourmet Swiss cuisine, and unforgettable mountain experiences.

meals.breakfast: Final full alpine breakfast at the B&B — a celebratory spread with champagne or prosecco, fresh pastries, local cheeses, smoked meats, and seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: Light lunch en route to the airport — stop at a premium restaurant in Chur such as Restaurant Stern or Zum Alten Zollhaus for refined regional cuisine and a farewell glass of Graubünden wine
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight premium dining (business/first class recommended for the return journey)

day_by_day.notes: Allow ample time for the transfer to the airport — mountain roads can be affected by winter weather conditions. Confirm your flight details and arrange private transfer pickup at least 4–5 hours before departure. Swiss customs allows generous allowances for food and wine purchases. Consider enrolling in a Swiss airport fast-track service for a seamless premium departure experience.
